Any local government that has a building code must adopt a minimum energy code when it updates its codes.

Several other codes apply statewide: the energy code (2012 IECC), the state plumbing code (2024 UPC), the state mechanical code (2024 IMC), the electrical code (2023 NEC) and the state fire code (2024 IFC). Local governments may adopt stricter plumbing/mechanical amendments and their own NEC amendments.

IA.notes: On 11/26/25 the building, fire, plumbing/mechanical and electrical rules moved from 661 IAC (Public Safety) and older numbering to 481 IAC (DIAL); older 661 citations are superseded. Energy code effective dates: r. 301.24/301.25 carry the ARC 9474C bracket (effective 9/10/25), but that is the date of the rule re-promulgation, not necessarily the first adoption of the 2012 IECC, so I left the field null. MO.model_note: Missouri has no statewide building, residential, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, fire or energy code for private construction. Counties, cities and fire districts choose and amend their own codes; a county that adopts a building code must use a 1999-or-later nationally recognized code.
MO.model_evidence_quote: Any community, if the community otherwise has the power under the law to adopt such an ordinance, may adopt or repeal an ordinance which incorporates by reference the provisions of any code or portions of any code, or any amendment thereof, properly identified as to date and source, without setting forth the provisions of such code in full.
MO.notes: Statutes checked: RSMo 67.280 (communities may adopt codes by reference; current version effective 8/28/2009); RSMo 64.196 ('any county seeking to adopt a building code ... shall ... adopt a current, calendar year 1999 or later edition, nationally recognized building code, as amended'); RSMo 67.281 (builders of one- and two-family dwellings/townhouses must offer fire sprinklers and purchasers may decline them, whatever the local code says). 2025-2026 bills (e.g., SB 743, SB 1431, HB 5770) proposed a 'Missouri Building Codes Act' and statewide commission. RSMo 67.283 and 8.363, which the bills would have created, do not exist on the Revisor site as of 2026-11-22, so they were not enacted. State-owned buildings: secondary sources say the Office of Administration (FMDC) applies I-codes to state buildings and the architects' board rule (20 CSR 2030-2.040) cites a 2018 IBC for evaluating designs where no local code exists. Neither was confirmed from an official adoption document, so no adoption is listed. The DNR directory lists locally adopted codes by county and city (it links to the State of Missouri Data Portal).

NE.model_note: Nebraska's Legislature adopts a state building code (2018 IBC, IRC, IEBC and UPC). It applies to state buildings and, by default, to any county, city or village that has not adopted its own conforming code, though not to farm construction. The 2018 IECC (Nebraska Energy Code), the 2023 NEC (through the State Electrical Act) and the State Fire Code apply statewide, with local enforcement allowed.
NE.model_evidence_quote: (2) The state building code shall be the building and construction standard within the state and shall be applicable: (a) To all buildings and structures owned by the state or any state agency; (b) In each county, city, or village which elects to adopt the state building code as its local building or construction code pursuant to section 71-6406 ; and (c) In each county, city, or village which has not adopted a local building or construction code pursuant to section 71-6406 within two years after an update to the state building code.
NE.notes: The editions are set directly in statute, not by agency rule, so the effective dates of the 2018 building code (Laws 2019, LB405 and others) are not stated on the statute pages and are left null. The NEC 2023 language came from Laws 2024, LB716. Bills to update the state building and energy codes in 2026 (for example LB800) were indefinitely postponed on 2026-04-17, according to non-official trackers; the official statute text checked on 2026-11-22 still shows the 2018 editions. Under 71-6406(4), local governments must notify the Department of Water, Energy, and Environment if they delete IBC chapter 13 or IRC chapter 11 (energy). Under 71-6406(6), local codes must be updated within two years after each state code update. The State Fire Marshal's posted Title 153 Chapter 1 PDF (sfm.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/title153-ch1.pdf) is an old 2001/2004 version listing older NFPA editions, so the fire code edition relies on the statute. A reviewer may want to confirm the current 153 NAC text on the Nebraska Secretary of State rules site. The 2012 NFPA 101 is recorded in the nfpa1 entry because the schema has no NFPA 101 family.

NV.notes: Effective date of the IFC: the approved regulation R205-24 says 'Filed February 27, 2026', and the LCB register index lists it as 'Approved by Legislative Commission 02/27/26'. OK.notes: The 2024 IBC, IRC, IEBC, IFC, IFGC, IMC and IPC took effect September 14, 2026 (43 Ok Reg, Number 20), replacing the 2018 editions. TX.model_note: In Texas, state law makes the IRC and IBC (as they existed on May 1, 2012) the minimum building codes only inside city limits. Cities enforce them, may adopt newer editions and may amend them after a public hearing. Unincorporated county areas have no state building code, but the state energy code and electrical code apply statewide, and licensed plumbers there must follow a board-adopted plumbing code.
TX.model_evidence_quote: Sec. 214.212. INTERNATIONAL RESIDENTIAL CODE. (a) To protect the public health, safety, and welfare, the International Residential Code, as it existed on May 1, 2012, is adopted as a municipal residential building code in this state. (b) The International Residential Code applies to all construction, alteration, remodeling, enlargement, and repair of residential structures in a municipality.

WI.model_note: Wisconsin writes and enforces its own statewide codes through DSPS. The Uniform Dwelling Code (UDC) covers new one- and two-family homes everywhere in the state. A municipality with delegated authority issues the permits and does the inspections; where none has it, DSPS or a state-appointed inspector does.

Where Can I Get a Permit? If the municipality covering your project location has been delegated authority to issue permits, and the project is not for a state-owned building or land, contact the municipality directly. Use the UDC Delegated Agent List to determine if your municipality has authority to permit and inspect your project. If your municipality does not have the proper authority, submit your application to DSPS via esla.wi.gov .

WY.model_note: Wyoming has no statewide residential building or energy code. The Council on Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety adopts the IBC, IEBC, IFC, IMC and IFGC as minimum fire and life-safety standards, which the State Fire Marshal enforces through plan review of public and government buildings. The NEC applies statewide to electrical installations. Cities and counties may take over enforcement if they adopt standards at least as stringent; houses are otherwise regulated only where a local government has adopted a code.
WY.model_evidence_quote: (a) The state fire marshal shall delegate complete authority to municipalities and counties which apply to enforce and interpret local or state fire, building, existing building standards or electrical safety standards which meet the requirements of this section.

The council rule also brings in IRC, IPC, IPMC and IECC provisions only as referenced in chapters 1-10 of the IBC/IFC/IMC/IFGC (Ch. 1 §2(a)(vi)). The agency says the 2024 I-codes were adopted June 28, 2024, but no official effective date was found, so effective_date is null. The council rule PDF is linked from the official wsfm.wyo.gov site and hosted on Google Drive; rules.wyo.gov was not checked. The NEC 2026 edition rests only on the agency's adopted-codes list, and a reviewer may want to confirm it against the Electrical Board rules (the linked Electrical Board rules PDF is a 2008 scan). W.S. 35-9-106(a)(i) caps council standards at those in the named I-codes.
